Samvardhana Motherson | Q1 FY27 Highlights

Financial Performance
- Revenue ₹35,244 Cr (+17% YoY | +3% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹3,096 Cr (+26% YoY | -18% QoQ).
- EBITDA Margin 8.8% (vs 8.1% YoY | 11.1% QoQ).
- PAT ₹1,076 Cr (+77% YoY | -31% QoQ).
- EPS ₹1.0 (vs ₹0.5 YoY | ₹1.4 QoQ).

Performance vs Estimates
- Revenue ₹35,243 Cr vs ₹33,777 Cr Est. (Beat).
- EBITDA ₹3,096 Cr vs ₹3,057 Cr Est. (Beat).
- PAT ₹1,032 Cr vs ₹1,008 Cr Est. (Beat).
- EBITDA Margin 8.8% vs 9.1% Est. (Miss).

Segment Performance

Wiring Harness
- Revenue ₹11,280 Cr (+10.2% YoY | +30.6% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹1,253 Cr (+7.1% YoY | +27.4% QoQ).

Modules & Polymer Products
- Revenue ₹16,695 Cr (-0.3% YoY | +11.2% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹1,144 Cr (-26.0% YoY | +19.4% QoQ).

Vision Systems
- Revenue ₹5,654 Cr (+2.2% YoY | +10.1% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹520 Cr (-15.8% YoY | +10.0% QoQ).

Integrated Assemblies
- Revenue ₹2,950 Cr (+2.5% YoY | +4.6% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹372 Cr (-16.9% YoY | +15.8% QoQ).

Emerging Businesses
- Revenue ₹4,795 Cr (-6.9% YoY | +29.5% QoQ).
- EBITDA ₹405 Cr (-45.6% YoY | +31.1% QoQ).

Management Commentary
- Record quarterly revenue achieved.
- Normalized PAT increased 55% YoY.
- Q1 Capex ₹1,614 Cr.
- FY27 Capex guidance ₹6,000 Cr (±10%) maintained.
- 13 manufacturing facilities under development.
- India remains a key growth market.
- Strong global order book supports outlook.
- Focus on operational efficiency and cost optimization.
- Geopolitical risks may pressure costs and freight.
- Global auto production outlook remains cautious.

Key Positives
- Record quarterly revenue.
- Strong YoY EBITDA growth.
- Robust PAT growth.
- Revenue, EBITDA & PAT beat estimates.
- Healthy India demand.
- Strong capex pipeline.
- Diversified global presence.

Key Concerns
- EBITDA margin missed estimates.
- Sequential decline in EBITDA & PAT.
- Margin pressure from raw materials.
- Weak global auto demand.
- Geopolitical uncertainties.

Key Monitorables
- EBITDA margin recovery.
- Global vehicle production.
- Raw material costs.
- Freight inflation.
- Capex execution.
- New facility ramp-up.
- Order book conversion.

Impact
- Positive.
- Strong revenue and earnings beat.
- Margin pressure remains manageable.
- Long-term growth drivers intact.
- India business continues to outperform.

Key Takeaway
- Samvardhana Motherson delivered a strong Q1 with record revenue and robust YoY earnings growth, beating consensus estimates on revenue, EBITDA and profit. While margins softened due to cost pressures and global automotive demand remains mixed, continued capacity expansion, a strong order book and healthy India demand support the company's long-term growth outlook.

Q1 FY27 | Midcap Growth Screen Highlights

Screen Criteria
- Market cap ₹20,000–60,000 Cr.
- Sales growth ≥25% YoY.
- PAT growth ≥25% YoY.
- PE ratio below 50x.
- Total shortlisted companies: 20.

Screen Methodology
- Midcap universe screened.
- Sorted into four valuation buckets.
- Focus on both growth and valuation.
- Cleaner starting point for research.

Next Research Steps
- Read management concalls.
- Analyze operating cash flows.
- Check base-effect sustainability.
- Assess earnings visibility.
- Evaluate growth sustainability.
- Track margin trends.
- Review order book and capex.

Excluded (PE >50x)
- Neuland Laboratories.
- Poonawalla Fincorp.
- Syrma SGS.
- Aether Industries.
- Piramal Finance.
- Acutaas Chemical.
- RR Kabel.
- Sona BLW.
- Craftsman Automation.

Important Exclusions
- MRPL excluded due to prior-year loss.
- HFCL excluded due to prior-year loss.
- Loss-to-profit transitions ignored.

For Financials & REITs
- PE not sufficient.
- Monitor asset quality.
- Track credit costs.
- Focus on ROA.
- Review occupancy levels.
- Monitor NOI growth.
- Track distributions.

Key Takeaway
- The screen identifies 20 midcap companies combining strong earnings growth with reasonable valuations. However, the screen is only the first filter—management commentary, cash flows, margin sustainability, and earnings visibility remain critical before making any investment decision.

Neuland and Gland tied up to make sterile APIs for microparticle depot injections. Depot injection puts drug inside tiny polymer balls so it releases slowly over weeks or months instead of daily doses 

Prostate cancer drug Lupron uses this method, and next generation GLP-1 obesity shots will move here too. Gland is building 1400 kg suite at Visakhapatnam to serve this niche. 

Fewer injections mean better patient compliance, which is why this segment is where premium injectable pricing sits 

premium injection 🙂 

Neuland is teaming with Gland to use Gland sterile API plant instead of building its own. Sterile drug plants are much harder to build than normal chemistry plants because everything needs to stay germ free during production. 

They need clean rooms, filtered air, and staff trained for aseptic work, so they cost hundreds of crores and take 3 to 4 years to get right. Neuland skips that build, Gland fills new capacity with steady API volumes, and both stay focused on what they know.

US passed BIOSECURE Act in December 2025 to stop federal money going to certain Chinese biotech and CDMO firms. 

That is pushing Western pharma companies to move orders out of China, and India is main destination because it already has US FDA cleared plants. Neuland Gland deal adds fresh sterile capacity aimed at these customers. 

Catch is Gland Pharma is owned by Shanghai Fosun, Chinese group. Some Western buyers may look past that, others will pause and ask hard questions during vendor checks.

ZERODHA CEO ON CLOSING AUCTION SESSION (CAS) 📊

• 🔔 Says CAS is not a bad idea and is widely used in global markets to improve price discovery and execute large institutional orders efficiently

• ⚠️ Recent sharp closing moves expose structural weaknesses in Indian markets rather than flaws in CAS itself

• 📉 Highlights that cash market short-selling remains difficult, while the securities lending & borrowing mechanism lacks sufficient depth

• 💸 Notes that higher STT and trading costs on futures have made options relatively more attractive, reducing arbitrage activity

• 👥 Despite over 13 crore registered investors, only 20–30 lakh traders actively trade daily, resulting in limited liquidity across cash, futures and ETFs

• 🏦 Adds that the rollout of CAS coincides with RBI's tighter capital-market exposure norms for banks, further affecting market liquidity

• 🛠️ Suggests improving short-selling, securities lending, market-making and reducing distortions between trading instruments to deepen Indian market

OCs expected this year span the last tower of Rising City Phase 1 (Ghatkopar), the North and Central towers of 25 South, Bel Air / Tower 1C at Hubtown Premiere (Andheri West), and multiple buildings at Hubtown Polaris (Ahmedabad) and North Star (Mehsana).

**Guidance: FY27 pre-sales of ~INR 6,000 Cr (H2-weighted on launch timing) and collections of ~INR 3,000 Cr. Annuity/commercial income to begin only after ~2.5 years; focus stays on the MMR region, with new projects pursued on an asset-light/partnership basis.**

**Outlook:** Hubtown is positioning around three levers, monetising a premium Mumbai-centric portfolio, consolidating marquee assets via Hubtown 2.0, and de-leveraging towards a net-debt-free balance sheet. Reported earnings will stay lumpy under project-completion accounting, and historically sub-10% ROE should improve as refinancing lowers the interest burden, price rises stick and deliveries pick up through H2. At CMP, the stock trades at ~1.2x P/B (book value ~INR 184), a modest multiple against a ~INR 11,583 Cr contracted pipeline yet to be recognised and combined post-merger GDV pegged at over INR 1 lakh Cr, though realisation of that embedded value hinges on NCLT approvals, execution and OC timelines.

**Hubtown Q1 Concall Snippets

Hubtown 2.0 Unlocks A New Growth Chapter**
Q1 FY27 marks the beginning of an inflection year for **Hubtown Limited (BSE: 532799; NSE: HUBTOWN; Market Cap: ~INR 2,660 Cr)**. Pre-sales of ₹535 Cr, up 8% year on year, demonstrate continued pricing power across their premium and ultra-luxury portfolio. This performance is anchored in a land moat that took 35 years to build. With ₹11,583 Cr of contracted balance revenue and three merger schemes progressing, FY27 is the year Hubtown's investment thesis begins to manifest in reported numbers.

**The Embedded Pipeline: Value Yet To Be Recognised**

The least understood part of the story is the embedded book. Across ongoing developments (including the to-be-merged entities), Hubtown has cumulative pre-sales of ~INR 14,835 Cr, of which ~INR 8,352 Cr is already collected and only ~INR 3,252 Cr recognised as revenue so far. That leaves ~INR 11,583 Cr of contracted pipeline still to flow through the P&L as projects complete and hand over, much of it already collected and simply awaiting the final milestone. Beyond this, Hubtown carries ~34 msf of planned development across 25 Chalet, 25 Estate, Season Phase 2, Sunstream City, Hubtown Commercial and Rising City, a multi-year growth runway to layer on top of a ~13 msf delivery track record built over three decades. The company was also the No. 2 top-selling residential developer in South Mumbai during the quarter.

**Hubtown 2.0: Consolidating The Marquee Assets**

The transformative piece is Hubtown 2.0, the amalgamation that consolidates the marquee luxury projects (25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South, effective 1 April 2025, subject to approvals) into the listed entity. The first two schemes have received key approvals and await final NCLT sanction, while the third is progressing through the regulatory process.

__Absorbing 4 promoter-group entities via NCLT to unify assets and eliminate cross-holdings.__

**Saicharan Consultancy:** Merging to boost Hubtown’s revenue share by 21.17% in the Ghatkopar Rising City project.

**25 West Realty:** Merging the luxury Bandra West asset to unlock a lifetime revenue potential of ₹6,000 crore.

**25 South:** Absorbing the 25 South Premium project with a Total Carpet area of 0.96 msf

**25 Downtown:** Large scale project in South Mumbai, in terms of revenue and area under development and total development of ~3.68 msf.

On completion, the ongoing development portfolio expands from ~7.13 msf to over 34 msf, backed by ~347 acres of landholding, with combined GDV expected to exceed INR 1 lakh Cr over time. Post-merger promoter holding moves to the ~68-70% range, as the schemes are issued against equity.

**Deleveraging And Refinancing In Motion**

Total borrowings have been cut to ~INR 5,181 Cr, of which INR 3,950 Cr sits in the to-be-merged companies and is project-linked and self-liquidating, funded directly by project cash flows. Legacy bank, NBFC and foreign-fund debt has been fully retired, and the company targets a net-debt-free balance sheet by FY2031. Management noted refinancing options improved sharply over the last quarter and it is looking to refinance ~INR 2,800 Cr of high-cost debt currently carrying 14-20% rates, with substantial savings expected once term sheets are finalised. All project surpluses remain ring-fenced towards debt repayment before any redeployment. On the capital side, enabling resolutions are in place for a preferential issue, QIP and FCCB (~INR 1,400 Cr / USD 150 Mn), with management preferring a single tranche once markets improve. Two promoter pledges remain outstanding, with release targeted within FY27.

**Pricing And Demand Hold Firm At The Top End**

Luxury demand and walk-ins stayed strong through a seasonally soft Q1, while mid-segment walk-ins were muted but conversion remained healthy. The higher floors (51st to 85th) of 25 Downtown will open strategically from October at premium pricing, with the typical higher-versus-lower floor gap running 30-40%, while 25 West has already risen INR 30,000-40,000/sq ft over ~1.5 years.

Jeena Sikho Lifecare Expands Wellness Footprint with New Integrated Centre in Manali

Jeena Sikho Lifecare (Shuddhi Ayurveda) has announced another expansion of its integrated healthcare model by establishing a premium wellness centre at Ajna Resorts, Manali through a long-term operating licence agreement.

While this isn't an asset acquisition, it is a capital-light expansion that allows the company to increase capacity without investing in real estate.

What's included?
The new wellness centre will comprise:
 - 30 luxury guest rooms
 - 5 consultation & treatment rooms
 - 5 dedicated spa therapy rooms
 - Retail area and allied operational facilities
The centre is expected to become operational within 60 days.

Investment Structure
Instead of purchasing the property, Jeena Sikho will operate the facility under a licence arrangement.
 - Licence fee: ₹7.66 crore (+ taxes)
 - Funded through internal accruals
 - No property acquisition or heavy capex
This keeps the expansion relatively asset-light while allowing the company to scale its wellness network.

Jeena Sikho has been steadily building an integrated ecosystem around Ayurveda, Panchakarma, preventive healthcare, and wellness retreats. Expanding into a destination like Manali gives the company access to a growing premium wellness tourism market, where customers increasingly seek longer-duration health transformation programs rather than standalone consultations.

The model also aligns with management's strategy of scaling through operating partnerships instead of owning hospitality assets, which could potentially deliver better capital efficiency if occupancy and patient inflows remain healthy.

The key monitorable now will be how quickly the company ramps up utilization at the new centre and whether this partnership-led expansion model can be replicated across other wellness destinations.

• Incremental FCNR(B) share vs deposit market share: Private Banks: 38.3% vs 35.7%; PSU Banks: 31.6% vs 58.2%

ICICI Bank: 13.2% vs 6.7%

Azad India Mobility: A Small EV Bus Player Positioned for India's Public Transport Transition 

India's electric bus ecosystem is still in its early innings, and Azad India Mobility is trying to position itself as a focused OEM rather than just another EV startup.

Some interesting takeaways:

🚌 Large structural opportunity
Government targets 50,000 electric buses by 2027

PM e-Bus Sewa plans deployment of 10,000 e-buses

🏭 Manufacturing expansion underway
The company has signed a lease agreement with Azad Coach Builders to establish an electric bus manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. 

📈 Financial inflection visible
FY26 reflects a sharp operational scale-up:

Revenue increased to ₹64.9 crore
Operating profit turned positive at ₹2.1 crore

Net profit improved to ₹2.37 crore

Fixed assets expanded 7x, indicating capex is now being commercialized.

A company worth tracking as India's public mobility ecosystem gradually shifts toward electric buses.

CITI ON BANKS

Key Takeaways:

• Bank-level data contradicts the market narrative that PSU banks would be the primary mobilizers under the FCNR(B) scheme

• Private banks mobilized US$10.7 billion (38.3% of net inflows), broadly in line with their deposit market share

• Foreign banks contributed US$8.4 billion (30% of net inflows), led by HSBC (US$6.1 billion) and Standard Chartered (US$1.86 billion)

• Despite holding 61% of deposits and 51% of FCNR(B) market share, PSU banks captured only 31.6% of net inflows

MORGAN STANLEY ON IGI

Recommendation: Overweight
Target Price: ₹462

Key Takeaways:

• Company reiterated its long-term growth drivers

• Certification market (by volume) is expected to grow at a 17–19% CAGR during CY25–30, as per management

• LGD (Lab-Grown Diamond) wholesale pricing has remained broadly stable over the last two years

• The industry is witnessing growers adding capacity after nearly three years, indicating supply expansion ahead

**Sedemac Mechatronics - R&D-led growth story
**
Sedemac’s journey started with sensor-less commutation (SLC) - its key technology moat that helped it scale rapidly in 2W/3W starter generators. Now, the same R&D engine is being leveraged to build the next layers of growth.

1. Core business still has runway: ISG penetration could rise from 40-45% → 55-60%, while Sedemac’s market share could expand from 36-38% → 46-48% by FY29.

2. EVs become the next growth engine: Its e2W/e3W motor controllers are expected to grow at a massive ~75% CAGR, potentially reaching 10-12% market share by FY29.

3. New growth layers are getting added: Sedemac is entering power tools, LCVs, CV after-treatment & EFI systems, while its genset business (~75% market share) continues to scale.

4. Capacity is being built ahead of demand: With existing plants at >90% utilisation, two new facilities should triple capacity, while Chennai land provides further expansion optionality.

HSBC expects FY26-29 Revenue / EBITDA / PAT CAGR of ~32% / 35% / 49%, with ROCE improving to ~29%.

The backbone remains R&D (~7% of revenue) allowing Sedemac to repeatedly build new products around its core technology.

Source - HSBC
